LESSON: WOOD

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Materials for production
Topic 3.1: Wood
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Wood, part of Materials for production in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is wood an important material day-to-day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Wood together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: learner develops technology skills when interacting and manipulating digital devices to search for

information on types of wood.

● Learning to learn: learner acquires skills of organizing own learning and works collaboratively with others as they reflect

on how different items are made from wood during visit to nearby workplaces.

Values:
● Unity as the learner cooperates with others when sharing digital and print media to search for information on types of

wood.

● Respect as the learner accepts diverse opinions when discussing methods of wood preparation.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCI’s):

● Environmental education and climate change: Learner understands the growth process of trees when using print or digital

media to search for information on the types of wood used at the workplace.

● Peer education and mentorship: Teamwork is enhanced when the learner participates the discussion on methods of wood

preparation for use in the workplace.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Social studies: as learner identifies the types of wood used at the workplace

Assorted Pieces of wood (hard and soft), career brochures, career magazines digital devices such as computer, laptop, smart
